content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Production WSGI and ASGI Servers for Flask"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"When deploying a Flask application to production, using the built-in development server (app.run) is strictly discouraged because it is not designed to handle high loads, concurrency, or security requirements. Instead, you need a dedicated production-grade WSGI (Web Server Gateway Interface) or ASGI (Asynchronous Server Gateway Interface) server."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding WSGI vs. ASGI in Flask"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Flask is fundamentally a synchronous WSGI framework. However, modern applications often require asynchronous capabilities for WebSockets, long-polling, or non-blocking I/O operations. Choosing the right server depends on whether your Flask app runs purely synchronously or leverages async routes and extensions."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Option 1: Gunicorn (WSGI)"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"Gunicorn (Green Unicorn) is a mature, widely used WSGI HTTP server for Python. It uses a pre-fork worker model, meaning a master process manages multiple worker processes to handle incoming requests."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Install Gunicorn using pip: pip install gunicorn"},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"gunicorn -w 4 -b 0.0.0.0:8000 \"app:create_app()\""},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Option 2: uWSGI (WSGI)"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"uWSGI is an extremely feature-rich, high-performance web server implementation that can act as both a WSGI server and a complete application server platform. It is highly configurable and ideal for advanced tuning."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Install uWSGI using pip: pip install uwsgi"},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"uwsgi --http 0.0.0.0:8000 --wsgi-file app.py --callable app --processes 4 --threads 2"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Option 3: Hypercorn (ASGI)"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"If your Flask application utilizes asynchronous routes (introduced in recent Flask versions) or you want to support HTTP/2 and WebSockets seamlessly, you should run Flask via an ASGI server like Hypercorn."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Install Hypercorn: pip install hypercorn"},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"hypercorn app:app --bind 0.0.0.0:8000"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Production Deployment"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always place a reverse proxy like Nginx in front of your Python application server to handle SSL termination, static file serving, and slow clients."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Calculate worker count using the formula: Workers = (2 * CPU Cores) + 1."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use process managers like systemd or Supervisord to ensure your WSGI/ASGI server automatically restarts on system reboot or application crashes."}]
